name: Gemini
tagline: Two-person crew; rendezvous and EVA practice
dispatch: The Gemini spacecraft was the first one Americans could actually fly. Mercury's astronaut mostly rode a capsule the ground controlled; Gemini's two-person crew got thrusters, a flight computer, and the ability to change their own orbit — to chase down another craft and dock with it. That was its entire reason to exist: not to go anywhere new, but to be a machine for practicing the maneuvers Apollo would need. Roomier than Mercury but still cramped, split into a crew module and an equipment section like Apollo after it, across ten flights it turned rendezvous, docking, and two-week endurance from open questions into things a crew could simply do.
description: The two-person spacecraft that taught NASA how to rendezvous, dock, and walk in space — the techniques that made Apollo possible. Ten crewed flights between 1965 and 1966, every one a step toward the Moon.
best_known_for: Two-person crew; rendezvous and EVA practice
